> Team Repository of the contest “Digital Mine on OpenEgiz”. **Replace the contents of this file with the instructions for your Submission.** The AI Jury runs the Submission strictly by these instructions, from scratch, in the Judge Environment. Accepted languages: English, Kazakh, Russian.

> **Start with the Concept**, the first section of [SUBMISSION.md](SUBMISSION.md): the Team writes it before any code. What AI agents build from this Template without a Concept is the Default Solution, published on the [contest site](https://openegiz-contest.github.io/) as the low bar: a Submission that does not go beyond it gets low levels in the Rubric. AI agents read [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md).

## Running

Requirements (Docker, `make`, Windows/WSL2 setup) are in [OPENEGIZ.md](OPENEGIZ.md) / [OPENEGIZ.ru.md](OPENEGIZ.ru.md).

```bash
sudo apt install -y make   # if make is missing (clean Ubuntu)
make up            # the OpenEgiz platform
make example-mine  # the Example Mine: twins, simulator, dashboard
```

Replace these commands with the commands of your Submission. The Submission must start by following these instructions without manual intervention (Rules, clause 6.4); downloading datasets and models and building are also listed here.

## What to open

- Grafana: the address and login are printed by `make up`.
- <where to see the mine visualization, which dashboards>

## Repository contents

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `team/` | Directory for the Team's code. Using it is optional: any part may be changed, including the platform core |
| `SUBMISSION.md` | Description of the Submission: **required** |
| `presentation.pdf` | Presentation: **required**, in the repository root |
| `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` | Instructions for your AI agents (Codex, Claude Code and others read them automatically) |
| `examples/mine/` | The Example Mine: shows how a digital mine is built on OpenEgiz. It is not a basis for the Submission |
| `OPENEGIZ.md`, `OPENEGIZ.ru.md` | Documentation of the OpenEgiz platform v1.0.4 |

The Submission is the `main` branch at the moment of the Freeze; other branches are not evaluated.

# SUBMISSION

<!-- Fill in every section. The AI Jury studies this file together with the code, the Build Report, the presentation and the Stand's interface. Accepted languages: English, Kazakh, Russian. These hint comments may be deleted. -->

## Concept

<!-- Written by the Team before the code: your own choice, a few sentences per answer. Everything else in the Submission follows from it. -->

**Enterprise:** <SmartMine AI is a fictional underground copper mine with tunnels, mining equipment, ventilation systems, and safety sensors. -->

**Users:** <Mine dispatchers, safety engineers, ventilation operators, and mine managers. -->

**Decision:** <The digital twin helps operators decide when to increase ventilation, stop equipment, or issue safety alerts based on simulated gas concentrations, temperature, and equipment conditions. -->

**Why this choice:** <Underground mining involves safety risks related to hazardous gases, ventilation failures, and equipment malfunctions. SmartMine AI will help simulate dangerous situations, monitor mine conditions, and support safer operational decisions.-->

**Real or fictional:** <SmartMine AI is a fictional underground copper mine inspired by real underground mining operations. Initial sensor values and equipment parameters will be simulated assumptions, with documented sources added for any real-world reference values. -->

## Team

<!-- GitHub usernames of the Participants. Other personal data are not required: the repository becomes public after the Freeze (Rules, section 15). -->

| GitHub |
|---|
|@aksezimmergenbaj-png |

## Mine

<SmartMine AI represents an underground copper mine focused on operational safety and ventilation monitoring.

The proposed digital twin includes:

1. Underground tunnels connecting mining zones and transport routes.
2. Mining zones where copper ore extraction is simulated.
3. Ventilation fans supplying fresh air to underground areas.
4. Environmental sensors monitoring gas concentration and temperature.
5. Underground mining vehicles transporting extracted ore.
6. A control dashboard displaying mine conditions and safety alerts.

The objects are connected through a simulated mine monitoring system. Sensors provide environmental data, ventilation fans influence airflow conditions, and equipment status affects mine operations.

The exact OpenEgiz twin definitions and source-code paths will be documented after implementation. -->
